phase3_findings.description: No default-run unit test checks that pyproject's core dependencies declare pymysql[rsa]>=1.1,<2 or that the empty mysql/all extras still exist; the deleted extras test is not replaced.
test_dependency_ci.py compares CI jobs and the PRFlow setup install with CONSTRAINED_INSTALL but not the AGENTS.md install command, so that command can drift unnoticed.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (suggestions and inconclusive checklist items below the important threshold)

The PR is ready to merge: no finding or checklist failure reaches the important threshold, and the remaining items are small test gaps, one inaccurate test comment, and three items the verifiers could not settle from source.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings and checklist items below the threshold, plus inconclusive items → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

1. `pyproject.toml` (lines 54-61): no test in the default `pytest -q` run checks that the core `[project].dependencies` declares `pymysql[rsa]>=1.1,<2`, or that the empty `mysql` and `all` extras still exist. The diff deleted `test_optional_database_drivers_have_exact_constraints`, which read the extras, and the lockfile guard only checks pyproject against the lockfile. (raised by 1/5 agents)
2. `tests/unit/test_dependency_ci.py` (lines 15-45): the test compares the three CI jobs and the `.prflow/config.json` setup install with the shared install command, but not the AGENTS.md *Commands* install command, so that command can drift without a test failing. Criterion 4 does not require this check. Checklist item VC-5 records the same gap. (raised by 1/5 agents)
- VC-20: FAIL (suggestion) — The comment asserts ImportError messages are a module name only, from a broken install missing a dependency. [tests/unit/test_cli.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  tests/unit/test_cli.py:1207-1208 comment says ImportError messages are 'a module name only'. src/sqllens/cli.py:144-145 echoes str(exc) verbatim for any ImportError (allowlist at cli.py:76-82), with no restriction on message shape. The comment is not true as stated: the test's own input (line 1211) is "No module named 'pymysql'", a phrase and not a bare module name. Other ImportErrors in the package carry free-text messages, e.g. src/sqllens/agent/integrations/mysql/sql_runner.py:60-61 'PyMySQL package is required. Install with: pip install pymysql' and chromadb/__init__.py:90. I did not trace whether any of these reaches _format_config_error from Config.load. The wrong statement is the comment's wording, and the unsupported part is the 'module name only' guarantee. The leak-safety conclusion (no config value in the message) is plausible but is not established by the comment's stated reason. Low impact, since the comment is only documentation.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

- VC-1: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — pymysql[rsa] extra exists in PyMySQL 1.1-<2 and pulls in cryptography, needed by caching_sha2_password on non-TLS connections [pyproject.toml]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  pyproject.toml:55 in the head view declares "pymysql[rsa]>=1.1,<2". The claim depends on PyMySQL's own metadata (the rsa extra and its cryptography requirement). No dependency_sources were supplied, and Globs for PyMySQL under site-packages in the repo directory and ~/.local found nothing. A filesystem-wide Glob timed out. PyMySQL source or metadata was therefore not read, and the claim could not be verified from the views alone.

  </details>

- VC-4: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — pytest.fail(..., pytrace=False) in a fixture produces a fail/error outcome (not skip) naming the setting [tests/connectors/_settings.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  tests/connectors/_settings.py:20 calls pytest.fail(f"{name} is not set; the connector suite requires it", pytrace=False), so the message names the setting. The claim depends on the installed pytest's _pytest/outcomes.py (fail accepts pytrace, raises Failed). The item has no dependency_sources and the views do not contain pytest. Globs of the worktree, /usr/lib/python3*, and ~/.local site-packages found no _pytest/outcomes.py. The library source could not be read, so the claim cannot be settled.

  </details>

- VC-5: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The four install commands (ci.yml unit/connectors/connectors-mysql84, .prflow/config.json, AGENTS.md) are identical and tests/unit/test_dependency_ci.py enforces it [.github/workflows/ci.yml]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  FAIL stored INCONCLUSIVE (requirement quote is missing): The commands are textually identical in ci.yml (lines 49,109,180), .prflow/config.json:105 and AGENTS.md.src:90. But tests/unit/test_dependency_ci.py only asserts the constant against the three ci.yml jobs (lines 15-21) and .prflow/config.json (28-33). It never reads AGENTS.md (grep for AGENTS in test_dependency*.py: no match), and does not compare the commands to each other beyond the shared constant. So the claim that the test enforces all four is false for AGENTS.md; AGENTS.md could drift unnoticed.

  </details>

</details>
